# Rohith Illuri

> Self-taught developer. Motto: "Deeds, not words" (facta non verba). The
> portfolio is a single static HTML page with a dark antiquarian aesthetic —
> no framework, no build step, no bundler.

## About

Rohith is a self-taught developer with no CS degree — every project below was
learned by building it. He likes shipping small, deliberate software,
performance work, and clean UIs. Outside of code: heavy lifting, AC/DC at
unreasonable volumes, and Tarantino films.

- Site: https://rohithilluri.github.io
- GitHub: https://github.com/rohithIlluri
- Email: rohith.illuri@gmail.com

## Sections

The page is structured as four numbered parts:

- **Part I · The Works** — the projects
- **Part II · The Craft** — the tools he works in
- **Part III · The Muses** — films and music that shaped the work
- **Part IV · The Letter** — how to get in touch

## Part I · The Works

- **Crave** — a marketplace for food: ordering, fulfilment, the whole road from
  hunger to table. React, Node, PostgreSQL.
- **CryptoApp** — live markets rendered as they move: prices streaming, charts
  breathing. React, WebSocket.
- **Toronto** — a city read through its data: patterns surfaced from the civic
  record. Python.
- **NNets** — neural networks built from first principles, no framework, only
  the mathematics. Python, Micrograd.

## Part II · The Craft

JavaScript · React · Node.js · Python · PostgreSQL · Docker · AWS · GraphQL

## Part III · The Muses

Films: Kill Bill, Pulp Fiction, Interstellar.
Sound: A.R. Rahman, AC/DC, The Beatles.

## How the site is built

A single `site/index.html` — inline CSS and inline JS, served straight from
GitHub Pages. Notable implementation details:

- **Living paintings** — each part sits over a public-domain painting from
  Wikimedia Commons (Cole, Raphael, Velázquez, Botticelli, Vermeer), layered
  over a pure-CSS "underpaint" gradient that renders even when the network or
  JS is unavailable. Images walk a fallback chain and remove themselves rather
  than leave a gap.
- **Motion posters** — six tilted, gilded cards for the muses.
- **Generative soundtrack** — Tone.js synthesizes an orchestral string loop in
  the browser (A minor, 80 BPM). No audio files, no autostart: it is gated
  behind an explicit click on the sound toggle.
- **Progressive enhancement** — nothing is hidden unless JS actually ran
  (`html.js` gates every reveal), and `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the
  embers, drifts and Ken Burns pans.
- **Scroll-driven CSS** — the progress thread runs on a CSS scroll timeline
  where supported, falling back to a rAF-throttled listener.
- **Locked-down CSP** — `default-src 'none'` with a narrow allowlist; the one
  CDN script (Tone.js) is pinned with Subresource Integrity.

## Tech

Static HTML/CSS/JS · Tone.js (generative audio, jsDelivr + SRI) ·
Google Fonts (Cinzel, EB Garamond) · Wikimedia Commons (paintings) ·
GitHub Pages (hosting) · GitHub Actions (test + deploy)

Source: https://github.com/rohithIlluri/rohithilluri.github.io
Structured data: JSON-LD (`Person`, `WebSite`, `ItemList`) is embedded in the page head.
